title: Deep learning detects slow slip events in Cascadia GNSS data
summary: A detector combining convolutional and attention-based neural networks, trained on synthetic geodetic time series, was applied to raw GNSS data in Cascadia from 2007 to 2022. The authors report 78 detections, including 35 of 40 events in the 2007–2017 comparison catalog and 43 additional events. Detection patterns align with tremor activity, but the paper says independent acquisition-data validation is needed, and shorter/low-confidence events remain uncertain. This method is specific to this station network and does not predict earthquakes.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network and Transformer attention model
organization: ISTerre, Université Grenoble Alpes; Université Savoie Mont Blanc; CNRS; IRD; Université Gustave Eiffel; GIPSA-lab, Université Grenoble Alpes; Grenoble INP; Institut Universitaire de France

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full text, abstract, methods/results, affiliations and publication history.

evidence.tested: Applied detector outputs were compared with a prior event catalog and tremor activity in real Cascadia GNSS data.
evidence.unknown: Some additional/short detections remain uncertain; article states validation with an independent acquisition dataset is needed. This is not earthquake prediction.
evidence.ai_role: A CNN plus Transformer trained on synthetic GNSS series classified slow-slip windows in raw multistation GNSS data and produced event detections.
